en.name: Our Lady of Medjugorje
en.summary: Reported apparitions beginning in 1981 to six young visionaries in a Bosnian-Herzegovinian village, among the most visited and most debated Marian sites of the modern era.
en.body: Starting in June 1981, six young people in the village of Medjugorje, in what was then Yugoslavia, reported the Virgin Mary appearing to them, delivering messages centered on prayer, fasting, conversion, and peace, and several of the visionaries have reported continuing to receive daily or periodic apparitions for decades since, an extraordinarily long duration unlike almost any other reported Marian phenomenon. The site grew into one of the most visited Catholic pilgrimage destinations in the world, drawing tens of millions of pilgrims over the following decades, even as the Church's official assessment of the apparitions' authenticity remained unresolved through multiple investigative commissions over many years. In 2024, the Vatican issued a formal note permitting pastoral and devotional engagement with the site's evident spiritual fruits, numerous reported conversions, increased prayer and confession, without pronouncing a definitive judgment on the supernatural authenticity of the ongoing apparitions themselves, a distinct and more cautious form of recognition than the full approval given to other sites in this catalogue.
